main_text.p: nemo autem potest esse & membrum,& Ca-put Ecclesiæ Catholicæ. Itaque Gregorius sic scribit: {a}ibid. E-pist.36.Vniuersa sibi tentat asscribere, & omnia, quæ soli vni Capiti cohærent, videli-cet Christo, per elationem pompatici fermo-nis, eiusdem Christi sibi studet membra subii-cere. Hæc Gregorius. Quibus verbis friuolum illud effugium de Capite ministeriali penitus disperdit. Nam si quis opponat, Romanum Pontificem esse Vicarium Christi, & Caput ministeriale: Responder Gregorius, soli vni Capiti tribuendum esse hunc honorem, non ergo Vicario: esse solum vnum Caput Eccle-siæ Catholicæ, non igitur locum esse Capiti ministeriali in Ecclesia vniuersa; neminem debere membra sibi eiusdem Christi subiice-[illegible, ~5 letters] Vicarium Christi, aut

page.notes: The printed text in the lower-left and right-edge fragments is partly illegible; the words are given as far as they can be read, with [?] where letters are doubtful. The "Quibus" word has a handwritten wavy underline in pencil or ink, which is not printed text. "Responder" is printed as it appears; it may be a printing error for "Respondet". The bottom left line is only partly readable; the first word is unread. The right-hand text is only a fragment at the edge of the scan and has been transcribed only as far as visible. The right-hand strip is cut off by the scan edge; its fragments are word beginnings and endings only, and are shown as read. The top line is cut off, so the word "Vicarium" is uncertain. The word "quę" is uncertain. The left margin notes have been placed at the beginning of the paragraph beside which they stand.
